Hon'ble Sameer Jain,J.
1.
Heard Sri Awadhesh Kumar, learned counsel for the applicant and Sri Rajendra Singh, learned AGA for the State-respondent.

2. The instant application has been filed seeking set aside the bail granted to O.P. No. 2 vide order dated 10.07.2024 passed by Additional Sessions Judge, Court No.6, Ghaziabad in Bail Application No.5871 of 2024 arising out of case crime no.272 of 2024, under Sections 420, 467, 468, 471, 406,
504, 506 IPC, P.S.- Nandgram, District- Ghaziabad.
3.

entities.text: Additional Sessions Judge, Court No.6, Ghaziabad
entities.label: COURT

sentences.text: Learned counsel for the applicant submits that applicant is informant of the case and he has moved the instant bail cancellation application on the ground that in spite of the fact that O.P. No.2 committed fraud and cheating, court concerned enlarged him on bail.

4. He further submits that there is evidence against the O.P. No.2 that he in spite of the sale-deed Rajkumar Jain vs State Of U.P. And Another on 13 September, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/43869656/
1 did not provide possession to the applicant and he also after sale-deed executed an agreement to sale to some other person and, therefore, it cannot be said that O.P. No.2 did not commit any offence.
He next submits, court concerned failed to properly appreciate the facts of the case and wrongly granted bail to O.P. No.2 and, therefore, bail granted to O.P. No.2 should be cancelled.

5. Per contra, learned AGA submitted that as per allegation, in spite of the sale-deed executed in favour of the applicant, O.P. No.2 did not provide possession of the property to him and he also subsequently, executed an agreement to sale in favour of some other person and, therefore, it cannot be said that he did not commit any offence of fraud and cheating.
6. Learned AGA however further submitted that all the alleged offences are triable by Magistrate-I Class and after considering entire facts of the case, court concerned enlarged him on bail.
7. I have heard learned counsel for the parties and perused the record of the case.

8. As per the applicant who is informant of the case,, without properly appreciating the facts of the case, court concerned enlarged O.P. No.2 on bail but from perusal of bail order dated 10.07.2024 passed by the court concerned, it reflects that it is a well reasoned order.
9. Further, the alleged offences are triable by Magistrate-I Class and, therefore, I don not find any good reason on the basis of which, the instant bail cancellation application can be allowed.

10. Law is settled that it is easy to reject a bail application but it is very difficult to cancel a bail already granted to an accused and for cancellation of bail, very cogent and over-whelming reasons must be present on record but in the present matter, I do not find any such cogent and over-whelming reason.
11. Therefore, in my view, the instant bail cancellation application is devoid of merits and is accordingly, dismissed.

Order Date :- 13.9.2024 S.A.
